title: Regional handoff safeguard and variant eviction controller
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a regional handoff safeguard that detects overloaded/degenerate regional pools (429 spikes, sustained timeouts, elevated error rates) and performs an orderly handoff to alternate regions or lower-cost model variants. Introduces a Variant Eviction Controller (VEC) that performs temporary soft-evictions (probation + decay) of model variants per-tenant and per-route, plus a circuit scoring system to decide open/half-open states. Goal: keep tenant requests served with minimal latency regressions while protecting regional capacity and SLOs.
design_decisions: Use a hybrid trigger stack: immediate hard triggers for large 429 bursts (rate * duration) + probabilistic soft triggers for sustained error-rate/timeouts using EWMA windows.
Maintain per-tenant and per-route circuit scores rather than only per-region — allows localized degradation without global switchovers.
Variant Eviction will be reversible via a decay-based probation window (configurable half-life) rather than permanent ban; supports automatic reinsertion when health returns.
Prefer staged handoff: 1) local variant swap -> 2) region reroute -> 3) tier downgrade. Each stage has backoff and telemetry checks.
All decisions are governed by a feature-flagged policy and an operator-visible audit trail (change reason, thresholds crossed, telemetry snapshot).
implementation_plan: Add scoring library to routing service to compute per-route/per-tenant circuit score (latency, 429 rate, 5xx rate, p95 tail).
Implement Variant Eviction Controller microservice with an HTTP/gRPC control API used by router to request variant swaps and to read probation state.
Wire telemetry -> scoring: extend metrics pipeline with short-lived TTL windows for burst detection and EWMA for sustained signals.
Feature flag default off. Roll out in stages: internal canary -> small set of low-risk tenants -> broad.
Create admin console view to visualize evictions, scores, and to manually force-recover variants.
Instrument end-to-end experiments and QA harnesses to simulate 429 bursts and timeouts across regions.
acceptance_criteria: Router can swap model variant for a route without dropping active requests (graceful switch, under 2s error impact in canary).
Circuit score generation aligns with offline reference implementation (unit tests + golden fixtures).
When a region reports 429>threshold for >30s, the system completes a staged handoff to alternate region/variant within configured SLO window.
Evicted variants auto-reinstate after probation decay if health metrics return to baseline, with audit trail entry for the transition.
Admin console shows per-tenant evictions and allows manual override; RBAC respects existing permissions.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): deploy VEC to staging and enable on internal alpha tenants. Exercise with load tests simulating 429 and p95 spikes.
Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5 internal customers and 2 test routes (feature flag + sampled traffic). Monitor error budget usage and latency shift.
Phase 2 (pilot): open to select external customers with SLA notification. Provide runbook and opt-out toggle per-tenant.
Phase 3 (general): enable gradually across regions with throttled enabling and an automated rollback if systemwide error budget crosses threshold.
Each phase guarded by SRE checklist (dashboarded metrics, runbooks, on-call confirmation).
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring logic with synthetic 429, timeout, and 5xx sequences.
Integration tests: end-to-end routing + VEC interactions in a local multi-region testbed.
Chaos tests: inject network partitions to verify graceful handoff and no-request loss during variant swap.
Load tests: sustained burst scenarios to validate EWMA soft-trigger behavior and hard-trigger thresholds.
Postmortem drills during canary to exercise operator workflows and rollback procedures.
